previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, bioprosthetic aortic valve, and prior TIA presented with a transient episode of vertigo and lightheadedness lasting less than five minutes. Imaging showed no acute intracranial hemorrhage or arterial occlusion, and the event was attributed to a posterior circulation TIA likely due to cardioembolic risk from subtherapeutic anticoagulation. Her INR had been subtherapeutic at 1.4 two weeks prior, and despite an increase to warfarin 3 mg, it remained low at 1.8 on admission. She was bridged with enoxaparin and warfarin was increased to 4 mg daily, achieving a therapeutic INR of 2.1 by discharge. Aspirin was discontinued to reduce bleeding risk. She remained neurologically stable, with no recurrence of symptoms, and was discharged home with close follow-up and stroke education.
